correctness.rationale: Coordinate color-exchangeability and Stirling partition count give P(X_i=X_j)=S(n−1,q)/S(n,q), and orthogonality between distinct cyclic character indices. Thus each nonconstant frequency block is (1+theta)I−theta J; its zero-sum and constant-coordinate eigenspaces yield all multiplicities and the q−1 nullity at n=q. Comparing onto configurations with extra symbols of two different colors proves strict positivity for n>q; n=q+1 and the fixed-q asymptotic follow directly from Stirling values/inclusion-exclusion. Independently computed nine exact/complex finite Gram matrices match the analytical spectrum. q need not be prime; finite spectra do not replace the all-(n,q) proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The all-degree Hamming-sphere result is broader in degree but not in sampling support, and regular combinatorial design/orthogonality existence does not imply the onto-support exact Gram spectrum. No broader same-domain theorem was encountered.

limitations: Degree-one character band only; general q cyclic alphabet, n≥q.
